* Unit tests using unittest, runnable via `python -m unittest`.
* Ten usage examples in `_examples()`.

"""
Thread-safe LRU cache with per-entry TTL, capacity eviction, injectable clock,
statistics, unit tests, and usage examples.

This module provides a single public class, `TTLLRUCache`, which combines:

* Least-Recently-Used (LRU) eviction when the cache exceeds a fixed capacity.
* Per-entry Time-To-Live (TTL) expiration, evaluated lazily on access and
  eagerly during maintenance sweeps.
* Full thread safety via a re-entrant lock guarding all internal state.
* An injectable clock so that time can be controlled deterministically in
  tests and simulations.
* Rich statistics: hits, misses, evictions, expirations, insertions, and
  current size / capacity introspection.

The implementation is dependency-free and uses only the Python standard
library. It is suitable for embedding in services that need bounded,
self-expiring in-memory caches without pulling in third-party packages.

Design notes
------------
* The cache is backed by a `dict` (for O(1) lookup) plus an intrusive
  doubly-linked list (for O(1) LRU reordering and eviction). Sentinel
  head/tail nodes simplify edge cases.
* Expiration is lazy: an entry is considered expired the moment its
  `expires_at` is <= the current clock value. Expired entries are removed
  on access, and a `sweep()` method is provided for proactive cleanup.
* The clock is a zero-argument callable returning a float (seconds). The
  default is `time.monotonic`, which is immune to wall-clock adjustments.
* All public methods acquire the internal lock, so the cache is safe to
  share across threads. Callbacks (if any) are invoked while holding the
  lock; keep them short and non-reentrant.
